perOption.label: (A)
perOption.reason: 'our attention tends to be directed outward': 'direct' is transitive and 'attention' is the theme, not the agent, so the passive infinitive after 'tends to' is required. Active 'tends to direct' would lack an object. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (B)
perOption.reason: 'While' is a concessive subordinator introducing a full finite clause ('this pattern of attention is necessary ...'), with the main clause 'it actually prevents ...' following. Structure Sub + S + V, Main S + V is complete. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (C)
perOption.reason: 'necessary when solving problems analytically' is elliptical 'when [one is] solving problems'. A hardline dangling-modifier objection exists (matrix subject 'this pattern of attention' does not solve problems), but generic-agent ellipsis with 'when + V-ing' is standard accepted usage in descriptive grammar and KSAT convention. Not a formal error.

perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: 'the connections that lead to creative insights': relative pronoun 'that' has plural antecedent 'connections' and functions as subject of plural verb 'lead'. Agreement and case both check out. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (E)
perOption.reason: Perception-verb complement: 'hear the quiet voices ... to tell us' violates the rule that hear + object licenses only a bare infinitive ('tell') or present participle ('telling'), never a to-infinitive. Rescue readings fail: a purpose infinitive ('in order to tell us') would make 'we' the understood teller, which is semantically incoherent; an adjectival infinitive on 'voices' ('voices to tell us') carries futurity/modality contradicting the intended simultaneous sense and is blocked inside the perception-verb complement anyway. Should be 'telling' (or bare 'tell').

note: Single clear violation at (E) via the perception-verb bare-infinitive/participle rule; alternative parses (purpose infinitive, adjectival infinitive) were actively tested and all fail. (C) invites a strict dangling-modifier quibble but generic 'when + V-ing' ellipsis is conventionally licensed, so it is not defensible as an answer. Answer uniquely (E), high confidence.
